rulings.reasoning: The customer only referenced account/card identifiers and intentions that are present in the governing scenario or supplied knowledge: card 9013, card 0767, checking account 5678, and a one-time payment. They did not assert any unsupported balances, dates, or prior actions.

The customer has not clearly confirmed a payment yet. They asked for options and then corrected the card, so they did not confirm before validated payment details were presented and confirmation was requested.
The customer continued pursuing a one-time payment from checking account 5678 and corrected the target card to 0767 rather than abandoning or replacing the goal.

The customer used the informal phrase “the usual amount” as the payment amount type, which is not a real listed payment option and required the assistant to explain available payment amount choices. This is material evidence of a fluency gap about payment_amount_type.

The declared correction was supposed to be an amount_type change from statement_balance to minimum_due. The observed correction was instead a card change from 9013 to 0767, and no amount_type correction to minimum_due has occurred.
